title: Private min pack: add GPU saturation dashboard + latency/error correlation panels
author: Sergio Costa
description:
Context: Private installs have been missing a consistent, day-1 view into GPU saturation that correlates with request latency/errors. Support has been relying on ad-hoc `nvidia-smi` screenshots and vendor-specific exporters, which makes it hard to triage prefill/decode slowdowns or rising 5xx due to OOM/backpressure.

This PR adds a new Grafana dashboard "Private / GPU saturation" built to work with the min-pack Prometheus expectations (DCGM exporter preferred; node-exporter optional for host context). It includes core GPU saturation signals (utilization/memory/power/thermal/throttling) and includes correlation panels that overlay GPU signals with gateway/runtime golden signals (RPS, p95/p99, 5xx, queue depth) to reduce time-to-diagnosis.

What’s included (high level): GPU overview row: per-node GPU utilization (avg/max), memory used vs total, memory copy utilization (where available), power draw & power cap, temperature, and fan speed. Throttling row: throttle reason breakdown (thermal, power, reliability) + clocks (graphics/mem) to identify cap-driven slowdowns. Host context row: CPU steal, node load, and NIC rx/tx for "is it host contention?" sanity checks. Correlation row: p95/p99 request latency (gateway) + 5xx rate overlaid with GPU utilization and GPU memory utilization; optional overlay with runtime queue depth (if runtime dashboard metrics are present).

Templating & conventions: Uses the same folder naming and variable conventions as PR-319/320 (cluster, namespace, instance/node, gpu, tenant, model, route where applicable). GPU panels are keyed to `instance`/node + `gpu` index; correlation panels use `route`/`model` labels from gateway/runtime metrics and avoid cross-product joins. Includes dashboard links to "Gateway / Service overview" and "Runtime performance" dashboards.

Metrics assumptions (documented in dashboard description + panel help): Primary source: DCGM exporter (`DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL`, `DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED`, `DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_FREE`, `DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE`, `DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_TEMP`, `DCGM_FI_DEV_CLOCK_SM`, `DCGM_FI_DEV_CLOCK_MEM`). Throttling reasons: `DCGM_FI_DEV_THERMAL_VIOLATION`, `DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_VIOLATION` (shown as rate/boolean depending on exporter version). Optional: `nvidia_smi_*` if customers use an alternate exporter; panels include a fallback query pattern guarded by `or` where safe.

Notes / gotchas: MIG: this dashboard does not attempt to do per-MIG-instance accounting (varies by exporter and label semantics). We surface a banner note and recommend using node-level GPU aggregate when MIG is enabled. Cardinality: no per-pod/per-container breakdown in this dashboard; instance+gpu is the maximum label granularity here. This is intentional for Private environments with constrained Prometheus resources.

Testing: Rendered via the dashboard build pipeline and validated via `grafana-dashboard-lint`. Queries were tested against staging Prometheus with DCGM exporter v3.1.x + kube-state-metrics.

Follow-ups (out of scope): Add alert rules for sustained GPU throttling / memory pressure (will land in the PrometheusRule bundle PR). Consider a separate "GPU per-model" view once model label propagation is fully validated across private runtime deployments.

Screenshots: (omitted from PR body; see CI artifact "rendered-dashboard" for the JSON + PNG previews).
commits: dashboards/private: add GPU saturation dashboard skeleton + variables
dashboards/private: add utilization + memory + power/thermal panels
dashboards/private: add correlation row with gateway latency/5xx overlays
lint: fix dashboard units, thresholds, and panel descriptions
changed_files: lib/templating/variables.libsonnet (reuse common instance/gpu variables; minor tweaks)
docs/dashboards/private-min-pack.md (add dashboard entry + required metrics list)
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Dashboard looks good and matches the minimum signals standard direction. Two asks: (1) please ensure units are consistent (W vs mW) across exporters; (2) add a clear note about MIG and label semantics so Support doesn’t assume per-slice accuracy.

Sergio Costa (author): Updated panel units to normalize power to W (divide by 1000 when exporter reports mW) and added a MIG banner note in the dashboard header + panel description for GPU util/mem panels.

Omar El-Sayed (review): The latency overlay is useful, but the query `sum by (route) (...)` + GPU util `avg by (instance,gpu) (...)` can mislead if operators pick multiple instances. Can we default the correlation row to a single instance selection (or annotate that overlays are not causality)? Also, can you add runtime queue depth overlay but keep it optional if the metric isn’t present?

Sergio Costa (author): Good call. I changed correlation panels to require `instance` selection (panel repeats by instance when multi-selected) and added a short note: overlay is for correlation, not attribution. Added runtime queue depth overlay behind `or vector(0)` and a panel help note indicating it appears only when `redwood_runtime_queue_depth` exists.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please remove any implicit threshold coloring that looks like an alert (red/yellow bands) unless it’s documented. We’ve had customers treat dashboard colors as paging criteria. Also, can we add a small panel for 'GPU memory pressure (used/total)' with a clear 'OOM risk' label but without a hard threshold?

Sergio Costa (author): Removed the red/yellow background bands. Added a 'GPU memory pressure' stat (used/total and %) with neutral coloring and text describing the OOM risk symptoms (5xx spikes, CUDA OOM logs, decode stalls) without prescribing a threshold.
Nadia Rahman (review): Minor: correlation panels should use `route` and `model` labels but avoid `tenant` by default to keep query cost down. Can we hide tenant unless explicitly selected?
Sergio Costa (author): Updated variables: tenant is now optional and defaults to 'all'. Queries don’t include `tenant` matcher unless selected.
Allison Grant (approve): Approved. Thanks for the MIG + unit clarifications.
Sean Gallagher (approve): Approved with the threshold/coloring changes.
release_notes: Private min pack: adds a GPU saturation Grafana dashboard with utilization/memory/power/thermal/throttling views and correlation panels for latency/error triage.
